title: Factorio performance staging exceeds the conservative Windows path budget

source_observation.environment: Exact 2.5.5 archive 03DFC05F94435FAACB86F19D1BF0BCD160C515C46B8372C483EEBAEB5208A41C, exact Factorio 2.0.77.84539, fresh no-reuse target calibration on Windows
source_observation.fact: The legacy performance harness placed Factorio write-data beneath a deeply named artifact run. Factorio exited with code 1 during new-map creation with no package, Lua, dependency, or assertion failure. The same immutable baseline and candidate archives passed after only the package-excluded staging path was shortened; the observed deepest temporary locale path was 257 to 259 characters, above the 240-character conservative budget.

reproducer.expected: Every performance execution uses a fresh context-bound compact scratch root whose projected Factorio temporary paths are at or below the conservative 240-character budget, then relocates raw artifacts to the content-addressed evidence root without loss.
reproducer.observed: At a normal deep artifact root, both baseline and candidate could silently exit while creating a map; a short artifact root or bounded compact staging passed the identical load. A fresh 104-row 2.5.5 no-reuse campaign then passed every automated row, including all six paired performance lanes.

stable_id_and_migration_impact: none; package-excluded Factorio staging-path custody and path-budget proof only
